**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • General limit: 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates, 35 mph on rural highways, 25 mph on urban highways.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted).
• Construction zones: 30 mph unless otherwise posted. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Regulations | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Back‑seat seats are mandatory for children under 13. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is prohibited (unless using a hands‑free system).
• Texting while driving is illegal. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (0.02% BAC).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights.
• “Yield” signs require slowing and yielding to traffic. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Headlights & Lighting** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Fog lights are allowed only on foggy days. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display a valid registration sticker.
• Towing regulations require proper equipment and safe loading. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Parking Rules** | • No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces (unless you have a permit), or on sidewalks.
• Parking on the curb is prohibited in many cities. | Local city ordinances | | **School Bus Laws** | • All vehicles must stop for a school bus with its stop sign extended and lights flashing.
• Failure to stop can result in a $1,000 fine. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Traffic Cameras & Speed Cameras** | • Many counties use speed cameras; fines are issued automatically. | County law enforcement websites | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | Texas Department of Insurance | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The primary legal source for all traffic laws. 2. **TxDOT Website** – Offers updates on road conditions, construction, and new regulations. 3. **Local County Sheriff’s Office** – Often publishes local ordinances and enforcement notices. 4. **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)** – Provides driver’s handbook and licensing information. --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a simple but effective safety measure. - **Avoid distractions** – especially cell‑phone use; use hands‑free if you must talk. - **Observe speed limits** – they’re strictly enforced, especially in construction zones. - **Be mindful of pedestrians and cyclists** – Texas has a growing number of bike lanes. - **Check local ordinances** – parking rules can vary widely between cities. If you need more detailed information on a specific topic (e.g., DUI penalties, toll roads, or commercial vehicle regulations), let me know!
